## Highlights

- **Packages now match the host distribution's own release.** `--target=auto`
  builds in an image of exactly that distribution and version: Debian 13 in
  `debian:13`, Ubuntu 26.10 in `ubuntu:26.10`, Linux Mint in its upstream
  Ubuntu release, Fedora in `fedora:<version>`, openSUSE Leap in
  `opensuse/leap:<version>`. Previously `ubuntu:latest` was used for every
  Debian-family host, so a package built on Mint 22.3 demanded glibc 2.43 while
  Mint ships 2.39 and could not be installed. Version-pinned images are never
  replaced by a family builder image.
- **SELinux hosts work.** The workspace is mounted with `:z`, so
  `/work/build.sh` is readable for the container. Without it every build on
  openSUSE Tumbleweed or Fedora stopped with "Permission denied" (exit code
  126).
- **Two more toolchain heals.** An unreadable lock file version 4 (Ubuntu 24.04
  ships cargo 1.75, git2pkg needs 1.89) is now handled like an outdated rustc:
  rustup is installed and the build retried in the same run. A compiler that
  rejects a C++23 feature (`std::ranges::to`) makes git2pkg install the newest
  `g++` the distribution offers (`g++-14` on Ubuntu 24.04) and export
  `CC`/`CXX` before the retry.

## Changes

- A project's own find module that cannot find a library
  ("could not be found with the bundled find module") is a missing dependency
  again, not an ABI conflict; only explicit ABI messages stop the build.
- CMake modules are additionally looked up through `lib<name>.so`, because some
  distributions ship the library without a CMake config file.
- Verification accepts a hit even when `find` exits non-zero (missing
  `/usr/local`, for example).
- `Neither X … nor Y can be found` becomes a dependency.
- Badge, social and third-party images are never staged as the application
  icon; the real icon now wins (the git2pkg package shipped a badge before).
- A manually saved log is no longer saved a second time by a retry, and
  collision suffixes count 2, 3, … instead of nesting.
- Closing the window right after cancelling a build asks about the cache again;
  the dialog text covers "not finished" instead of "failed".
- C++ compiler problems and lock-file problems are reported with their real
  cause instead of "unknown error".

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/hyalcin70/git2pkg/compare/v0.2.0-alpha.35...v0.2.0-alpha.36
